reviews.body:
This appears to be fixed in `v4.7.0` of the `opensearch-go` client, with the inclusion of a short-lived `Context` attribute. 

See https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/443927db1f7b94d0eebce95ccb7c85ea631c6c7e/opensearchutil/bulk_indexer.go#L86-L88

In addition to the `worker.run` now allowing a context to be passed in:

https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/443927db1f7b94d0eebce95ccb7c85ea631c6c7e/opensearchutil/bulk_indexer.go#L406-L407

I'd prefer if this PR rather upgraded to the latest version of `v4` on `v4.8.2` (see https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/v4.8.2/CHANGELOG.md) and migrated over the tests in `integration_test.go` to account for the deprecations + changes.

Appears that this new approach will panic if we pass in an already cancelled `context.Context` to the `NewBulkIndexer`. I've opened an issue upstream for this https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/issues/1392

Also, this needs to run `make deps` or `go mod tidy` since it seems the `go.sum` is stale.

review_comments.body:
nit: Upgrading the dependency should probably be in the `Changed` section (which should be before `Fixed`):

```md
### Changed

- upgrade `opensearch-go` from `v4.7.0` to `v4.8.2` @pcbeingused333 
```

Then we can remove the `(upgrades ...)` trailer
Want to just confirm: have you run these locally?
FYI this panics when the timeout is `0` and workers are greater than 1 -- since the upstream bulk indexer appears to have a bug.

IMO this entire test can be replaced with a simple additional integration test:

```go
func testOpenSearchInterruptWrite(urls []string, client *osapi.Client, t *testing.T) {
	ctx, done := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second*30)
	defer done()

	m := outputFromConf(t, `
index: does_not_exist
id: 'foo-${!count("interruptWriteTest")}'
urls: %v
action: index
`, urls)

	require.NoError(t, m.Connect(ctx))
	defer func() {
		require.NoError(t, m.Close(ctx))
	}()

	cancelCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	cancel()
	err := m.WriteBatch(cancelCtx, service.MessageBatch{
		service.NewMessage([]byte(`{"message":"hello world","user":"1"}`)),
	})
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
}
```

comments.body: Thanks, agreed. Upgraded to v4.8.2 and switched to `BulkIndexerConfig.Context` (the regression test still fails on v4.8.2 without it, so setting the context is still needed). Migrated `integration_test.go` to the generic `Do`; the docker integration tests compile but I could not run them here.

Pushed a fix for the panic. An early `ctx.Err()` check alone would still leave a window if the context is cancelled while `NewBulkIndexer` is starting its workers, so the indexer now gets a context that is only linked to the batch context (`context.AfterFunc`) after the constructor has returned. I also ran `go mod tidy`, moved the bump to `Changed` (it is `v4.5.0` to `v4.8.2`, since that is what `main` has) and replaced the unit test with your integration test.

On your question: no, the integration tests have not been run yet. They compile and vet clean, and the cancelled-context case was checked with a temporary unit test (panics before this commit, passes after). Note that the new integration test covers an already cancelled context, not cancellation while a request is in flight.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
